narrative.northStar: The man page for your running product
narrative.overview: The console reads like a page from a Unix manual. Each route is one page with a NAME, an optional SYNOPSIS that states how the data gets there, and then its own sections (STATUS, EVENTS, ACCOUNTS, OBJECTS). A running header and footer frame every page, and the index lists sections by man-section number (users(5), settings(8)). It deliberately avoids the stock SaaS admin look: no gray sidebar slab, no KPI card row, no rounded cards. The owner scans, acts, and leaves.
keyCharacteristics: White paper, near-black ink, and one reserved accent.
Monospace for data, labels, controls, and section heads. Grotesk for sentences.
Hairline rules instead of containers, and zero radius everywhere.
Text controls in brackets ([ refresh ]) that invert on hover, like a terminal selection.
Figures right-aligned against the margin on dotted leaders.

rules.name: The Reserved Ink Rule
rules.body: The accent marks only the current page, links and primary controls, focus, and live state (healthy status dots). Roles, badges, and decoration stay ink.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from weight, case, and rules, not from gray fills or extra hues. Red is the only other color, and only for failure.

dos: Do set every new route as a ManPage with NAME, a truthful SYNOPSIS (loader → server function → binding), then its own Sections.
Do put real binding data on screen, and say plainly when something is empty.
Do keep page actions as bracketed controls on the NAME row.
Do run every motion on the single constant --dur (160ms, expo ease-out). It drops to 0 under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use cards, gray panels, KPI tiles, or rounded corners.
Don't spend the accent on decoration, roles, or badges.
Don't add icon tiles or glyph icons. Words and section heads carry meaning here.
Don't use eyebrow or kicker labels above headings. Section heads sit beside their content, not above titles.
